Method of Attack: Ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation recruiting affiliates to perform corporate breaches and encrypt devices
Highly customizable ransomware with command-line driven, human-operated execution
Uses different encryption routines (Full, Fast, DotPattern, Auto, SmartPattern) and encryption algorithms (ChaCha20, AES)
Spreads using domain credentials and PSExec to copy and execute ransomware on other network devices
Terminates processes and Windows services that could prevent encryption
Clears Recycle Bin, deletes Shadow Volume Copies, scans for network devices, connects to Microsoft clusters
Uses Windows Restart Manager API to close processes or services locking files
Uses access-token argument to secure negotiation chat access
Triple-extortion tactic: steals data before encrypting, threatens to publish data and DDoS victims if ransom not paid
Attack Vector: Use of domain credentials and PSExec for lateral movement and remote execution
Indicators of Compromise: Tor payment sites with black cat favicon
Data leak sites with bloody dagger favicon
Ransom notes named in format 'RECOVER-[extension]-FILES.txt' (e.g., RECOVER-bleepin-FILES.txt)
Unique Tor sites and data leak sites per victim
Ransom demands ranging from $400,000 to $3 million payable in Bitcoin or Monero
Affiliate console-based user interface showing encryption progress
